Q: Offset pagination returns empty page before reaching total count A: 



I initially suspected a client-side and tested the same request directly in the browser console
fetch("/api/conversations?offset=28&limit=28&order=updated&visible_only=true", {
credentials: "include"
})
.then(r => r.json())
.then(x => console.log("items=", x.items.length, x))
.catch(e => console.log(e));
Result:
items= 0
{ items: [], total: 28, limit: 28, offset: 28 }
So the second request is definitely being sent and answered, and this does not appear to be a CEF / JS-injection issue.
Also, although I previously observed total = 29, the same request shape now consistently reports total = 28. Page 1 returns 28 items, and page 2 (offset = 28) returns 0 items.
So the situation is:
- earlier observation suggested 29 total items
- current, direct request reports 28 total items
- last page is empty

Q: Creating clickable link to text file in Powershell A:

Direct string replacement can be done using -replace <regex>, <subst>:

$url = "file:///" + ($path -replace "\\", "/")

But it would be more correct to URL-encode each component individually:

$url = "file:///" + (($path -split "\\" | % {[uri]::EscapeUriString($_)}) -join "/")

Note that the URL syntax is scheme: //host /path. For file: URLs, the host name can be left empty, but you still need the correct amount of slashes – two to indicate that the (empty) host follows and one to indicate that the path follows.

file:///C:/foo/bar

It is also syntactically valid (though rare and not always supported) to leave out the //host part completely, keeping only a single slash to indicate that the /path follows:

file:/C:/foo/bar

But if you write file://C:/foo/bar, that would mean C: is the hostname. Some programs will understand it regardless, but some won't – Windows Terminal will not.

To make a link with custom text:

$ESC = [char] 0x1B

echo ("$ESC]8;;" + $url + "$ESC\" + "Hello" + "$ESC]8;;" + "$ESC\")
